answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because ridge only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, harbor is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any velvet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
